3. Description of Supplies and/or Services:

The Administration for Children and Families (ACF) requires specialized instructional systems design, curriculum finalization, digital learning integration, pilot facilitation, and knowledge-transfer services to complete, refine, and transition the enterprise "ACF Lead Forward Leadership Development Framework" for non-supervisory employees.

- Scope: The contractor shall finalize the remaining 15% to 20% of the active framework, including modular curriculum guides, participant workbooks, behavioral assessment rubrics, and SCORM/Section 508-compliant e-learning assets formatted for the HHS Learning Management System (LMS). The effort incorporates the vendor's preexisting, proprietary models (leaderLife®, SBFI Feedback Model, GROWTH Coaching Model, and GET REAL).
- Transition & Data Rights: The contractor must execute Kirkpatrick Level 1–3 pilot evaluations, deliver "Train-the-Trainer" certifications for ACF University staff, and provide a complete Technical Data Package (TDP) containing all raw, editable digital source files with perpetual Government-purpose data rights to ensure long-[REDACTED] m agency independence.
- Period of Performance and Contract Structure: This requirement is a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) commercial procurement valued at [REDACTED]. The period of performance is a twelve (12) month base period with no option periods.

V. Demonstration that the contractor's unique qualifications or nature of the acquisition requires the use of the authority cited above (applicability of authority).

USAFADS leadership sought an off-station training location that could satisfy the requirements necessary for annual training. Spaceport America Airfield was selected by the USAFADS/CC and COMACC as the winter training location for the Air Force Thunderbirds because the airfield meets the requirements outlined in ACCI 11-245, Para. 3.3.3.1. Off-Station Training. The USAFADS should conduct off-station training (away from Nellis AFB) during the training season to exercise the deployed operations aspect of their mission. The following factors should be considered when choosing a training location: logistical support, lodging proximity, limited public impact, sole-use airspace, over-the-field (OTF) flying training, and sufficient facilities for aircraft maintenance, operations, and training. IAW ACCI 11-245, the USAFADS training period occurs from mid-November to mid-March and is set aside for training new pilots. Due to competing mission requirements and flying schedules at Nellis AFB, the USAFADS can only conduct training in January. The USAFADS requires a location that has minimal precipitation and convective activity and at least 9 hours of civil daylight and a cloud ceiling of <12,000 AGL and winds > 15 kts. Climate data during winter indicated the best locations for this requirement lie within the southwest United States.

The USAFADS/CC conducted a Geographic Information System (GIS) assessment, IAW ACCI 11-245, of potential airfields in the southwest United States and narrowed the options to 12 potential airfields, excluding fields with scheduled air carrier service and significant military operations. The USAFADS conducted conversations with airfield managers at these locations to determine a potential source, and the majority of Contractors were non-responsive. Additionally, the USAFADS is required to conduct a site survey of the airfield to determine that it meets the necessary requirements. USAFADS conducted a site visit at the two locations that were responsive, to include the location at Spaceport America Airfield and Ft. Huachuca/Libby Army Airfield.

The location at Spaceport America in Truth or Consequences, New Mexico was selected because it meets all of the following requirements: 6,000 square miles of restricted airspace, low population density, a 12,000-foot by 200-foot runway, and low humidity, and the climate meets requirements for safe training operations during the winter. Additionally, there are no other uses of this airspace during the required time frame each year. USAFADS requires sole-use airspace for the duration of the training session with the ability to conduct training with no outside/unauthorized visitors and guaranteed flight times to ensure the USAFADS will be guaranteed 24 uninterrupted sorties for Team (1-6) with an additional 24 single-ship sorties. This is the only airfield that is able to provide all of the above to include climate requirements, services, airspace, and security. Spaceport America airfield is the only location that has the proximity to a F-16 base for maintenance and logistical support and an emergency cable divert to Holloman AFB, NM, which is required IAW ACCI 11-245. Additionally, the location is within the confines of White Sands Missile Range, which de-conflicts airspace scheduling because Temporary Flight Restrictions (TFRs) with the FAA are not required, as the Spaceport airspace location is already established within a restricted area.

Without this location, the USAFADS will not have the ability to practice 2-3 times a day with untethered conditions with unlimited and infinite airspace while allowing the team to use facilities for storage, maintenance and ops briefings, as compared to 1-2 times per day at alternative locations. Therefore, the demonstration and team members would not be able to become COMACC certified by March per year, as required of USAFADS personnel.
